summary: Defines a Link-attributes sub-TLV carried inside TLV 22 to flood certain link characteristics in IS-IS. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary:
IS-IS is a routing protocol in which every router floods a description of its own links to the rest of the area. The descriptions are built from small variable-length records called TLVs, each with a type, a length and a value.

This RFC adds one more record: a Link-attributes sub-TLV that sits inside the TLV that carries reachability information. It has two flag bits. One says the link has local protection, so a fast repair path can be set up. The other says the link must not be used when another router computes a repair path.

questions: what is the is-is link attribute sub-tlv
what does the local protection available bit mean
subtitle: A small sub-TLV that lets IS-IS routers advertise what their links can and cannot do.

tldr.problem: IS-IS floods link descriptions so every router in an area can compute paths. Some link characteristics, such as whether a link is protected or must be left out of repair paths, had no way to travel with the link description.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a Link-attributes sub-TLV carried inside the extended IS reachability TLV, type 22. It holds a 16-bit flags field with two defined bits, and a router that does not understand it simply ignores it.
tldr.outcome: Routers can flood and act on the new bits without any change to older routers. RFC 9650 later updated the registration procedure for the neighbour link-attribute bit values.

today: RFC 5029 is a Proposed Standard that has not been obsoleted, but it was updated by RFC 9650, which revises the registration procedures for the IS-IS neighbour link-attribute bit values.

sections.title: Where the Sub-TLV Fits
sections.content:
IS-IS, as specified in ISO 10589 with the IPv4 extensions in RFC 1195, has a router advertise one or several Link State Protocol data units. Those data units are composed of variable-length tuples called TLVs, of Type-Length-Value form.

RFC 3784 defines a set of new TLVs whose aims are to add more information about link characteristics, increase the range of IS-IS metrics, and optimise the encoding of IS-IS prefixes. This document defines a new sub-TLV named Link-attributes, carried within the extended IS reachability TLV, which is type 22.
sections.plainLanguage: IS-IS routers advertise their links in Link State Protocol data units, which are lists of TLVs. The new record travels inside the TLV that lists which neighbours are reachable.

sections.title: Requirement Words
sections.content: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED, MAY and OPTIONAL in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119. Those capitalised words set how strongly each rule applies.
sections.plainLanguage: The document uses the standard capitalised words for rules, so a reader can tell which parts are mandatory and which are advice.

sections.title: The Sub-TLV Format
sections.content:
The link-attribute sub-TLV is carried within the TLV 22 and has a format identical to the sub-TLV format used by the Traffic Engineering Extensions for IS-IS: 1 octet of sub-type, 1 octet of length of the value field of the sub-TLV, followed by the value field, which in this case is a 16-bit flags field.

The link-attribute sub-type is 19 and the link-attribute has a length of 2 octets. This sub-TLV is OPTIONAL and MUST appear at most once for a single IS neighbour. If a received Link State Packet contains more than one Link-Attribute Sub-TLV, an implementation SHOULD decide to consider only the first encountered instance.

Two bits are defined. Local Protection Available (0x01) means the link is protected by means of some local protection mechanism, such as the one in RFC 4090. Link excluded from local protection path (0x02) means this link SHOULD not be included in any computation of a repair path by any other router in the routing area. The triggers for setting up that bit are out of the scope of this document.
sections.plainLanguage: The record is four bytes: a type byte that says it is the link-attributes record, a length byte, and two bytes of flags. Two flags are defined, one saying the link has a fast protection path and one saying other routers should keep the link out of their repair paths.

sections.title: Interoperability with Older Routers
sections.content: A router that does not support the link-attribute sub-TLV will simply ignore it silently. No negotiation is needed and no failure results from an older router seeing the record.
sections.plainLanguage: An older router that does not know this record skips it. That is all the compatibility work the record needs.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content:
IANA has assigned codepoint 19 for the link-attribute sub-TLV defined in this document and carried within TLV 22. IANA has also created a registry for bit values inside the link-attributes sub-TLV. The initial contents of that registry are the value 0x1 for Local Protection Available and the value 0x2 for Link Excluded from Local Protection, both referencing this document.

Further values are to be allocated by the Standards Action process defined in RFC 2434, with early allocation, as defined in RFC 4020, permitted.
sections.plainLanguage: The record type and each of its flag bits get a number from IANA, so that different vendors agree on what each number means.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Any new security issues raised by the procedures in this document depend on the opportunity for Link State Packets to be snooped and modified, and the ease or difficulty of that has not been altered. Because the packets may now contain additional information about router capabilities, that information also becomes available to an attacker.

Specifications based on this mechanism need to describe the security considerations around the disclosure and modification of their information. The document notes that an integrity mechanism, such as the one defined in RFC 3567, should be applied if there is a high risk resulting from the modification of capability information.
sections.plainLanguage: Link State Packets can already be read and changed on the network, and this record does not change that. It does reveal a little more about what the routers can do, so the RFC says an integrity check is worth adding where that matters.

fields.name: Sub-TLV Type
fields.desc: Identifies the record. The value assigned by IANA for link-attributes is 19.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Length in octets of the value field that follows.

fields.name: Link-attribute Flags
fields.desc: Bit field. Defined bits: Local Protection Available (0x01) and Link excluded from local protection path (0x02).

items.label: Local Protection Available
items.desc: The link is protected by some local protection mechanism.

items.label: Link Excluded from Local Protection
items.desc: Other routers in the routing area should not include this link in a repair path computation.
